# Initial Setup

## Analysis setup

Data from the Forward Testing Effect (hereafter FTE) study can be accessed at an anonymized repository at: https://osf.io/jyrq8/?view_only=ede69ce309484a40bc50904358e7abb7.

Most of the data setup follows `FTE14a__mother_script.Rmd` found in the original repository.

```{r setup, error=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# 1. Set paths to specific folders in the working directory
data.path <- "data/"

# 2. Load packages
packages <- c("knitr", "tidyverse", "psych", "ggplot2", "rstatix", "doParallel", "car",
              "kableExtra", "mediation")

# automatically tries to retrieve packages that are not yet installed.
package.check <- lapply(packages, function(x) {
  if (!require(x, character.only = TRUE)) {
    install.packages(x, dependencies = TRUE)
    library(x, character.only = TRUE)
  }
})

# 3. Load data
df <- read.csv2(file.path(data.path, "fet14a_data_osf.csv"))

# 4. Some general settings that can be kept constant
# general behavior of chunk (outputs)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  warning = F, # suppress warnings and 
  message = F  # messages 
  )

# kable output 
options(knitr.kable.NA = '')

# settings to run analyses on multiple cores
no.cores = parallel::detectCores() - 4  # 8
cl = makeCluster(rep("localhost", no.cores))  # run all workers on local machine, 8 times
```

## Data preparations

`practice_type` is treated as a factor and change in cognitive effort is calculated as the difference score between `cognitive.effort_text1` and `cognitive.effort_text3`. `practice_type_bi` is a dummy variable with Restudy = 0, Retrieval = 1.

```{r data preps}
# Create factor and DeltaCE (cognitive.effort_diff)
df <- df %>%
  mutate(
    practice_type = factor(practice_type, levels = c("Restudy", "Retrieval")),
    cognitive.effort_diff = cognitive.effort_text1 - cognitive.effort_text3)

# Data cleaning to create dummy variable for practice type
df <- df %>%
  mutate(practice_type_bi = ifelse(practice_type == "Restudy", 0, 1))

# Create gender dummy variables for descriptive statistics and mediation analysis
df$male <- ifelse(df$gender == "male", 1, 0)
df$diverse <- ifelse(df$gender == "diverse", 1, 0)
```

## Data exclusion

Participants were excluded following the original FTE study if participants reported

- high disturbance (> 7) and low concentration (< 4) ($n = 8$),
- use of external help (e.g., taking notes) ($n = 8$),
- same study participation ($n = 4$), or
- language other than German ($n = 13$).

In total, data from 33 subjects were excluded from our analysis. 

```{r exclusion}
# Filter a subset of subjects based on exclusion criteria 
Excl <- df %>%
  mutate(
    Excl_dist = disturbed > 7 & concentration < 4, 
    Excl_help = external.help == "yes",
    Excl_same.study = participated.before == "I have participated at the SAME study before.",
    Excl_language = language == "other") %>%
  
  filter(Excl_dist == T | 
           Excl_help == T |
           Excl_same.study == T | 
           Excl_language == T)

# Apply exclusion criteria
df <- df %>%
  filter(!(ID %in% Excl$ID))  # 308 -> 275
```

## Descriptive statistics (Table 1)

Below are descriptive statistics of variables used in further analyses (presented as Table 1 in the manuscript).

```{r, overall sample}
# Overall sample
library(psych)
describe(df[, c("practice_type_bi", "cognitive.effort_diff", 
                "cognitive.effort_text1", "cognitive.effort_text3",
                "test.final_text3_sum", "interest_text1", 
                "prior.knowledge_text1", "episodic.memory_acc",
                "sellmo_learninggoals", "male", "diverse", 
                "age")])[, c(2:5, 8:9, 11:12)]
```

```{r, by practice type}
# Descriptive statistics by practice type
describeBy(df[, c("cognitive.effort_diff", "cognitive.effort_text1", 
                  "cognitive.effort_text3", "test.final_text3_sum", 
                  "interest_text1", "prior.knowledge_text1", 
                  "episodic.memory_acc", "sellmo_learninggoals", "male", 
                  "diverse", "age")], df$practice_type)
```
Also, covariate distributions are compared for balance between the restudy and retrieval conditions. Other than key variables, the covariates do not show meaningful differences between the practice type conditions.

```{r, two-sample t-tests for covariates}
# Two-sample t-tests for comparing covariate distributions by practice type
t.test(cognitive.effort_diff ~ practice_type, data = df, 
       var.equal = FALSE)  # t(261.71) = 2.074, p = 0.039
t.test(cognitive.effort_text1 ~ practice_type, data = df, var.equal = FALSE)
t.test(cognitive.effort_text3 ~ practice_type, data = df, 
       var.equal = FALSE)  # t(272.49) = -1.825, p = 0.069
t.test(test.final_text3_sum ~ practice_type, data = df, 
       var.equal = FALSE)  # t(272.66) = -2.970, p = 0.003
t.test(interest_text1 ~ practice_type, data = df, var.equal = FALSE)
t.test(prior.knowledge_text1 ~ practice_type, data = df, var.equal = FALSE)
t.test(episodic.memory_acc ~ practice_type, data = df, var.equal = FALSE)
t.test(sellmo_learninggoals ~ practice_type, data = df, var.equal = FALSE)
t.test(male ~ practice_type, data = df, var.equal = FALSE)
t.test(diverse ~ practice_type, data = df, var.equal = FALSE)
t.test(age ~ practice_type, data = df, var.equal = FALSE)
```


# Mediation Analysis

## Mediator model specification
Retrieval leads to less change in cognitive effort (cognitive effort after learning block 1 - after learning block 3), supporting the first part of the encoding hypothesis.

```{r, mediator model}
# Mediator model
med.fit <- lm(cognitive.effort_diff ~ practice_type_bi, data = df)
summary(med.fit)
```

## Outcome model specification (Table 2)

We examine interest (`interest_text1`), prior knowledge (`prior.knowledge_text1`), episodic memory (`episodic.memory_acc`), learning goals (`sellmo_learninggoals`), as well as some demographics (`gender`, `age`) as potential confounders.

mediation::mediate() does not work well with factors with more than two levels. Therefore, we replace `gender` with dummy indicators `male` and `diverse`, leaving `female` as the reference group.

```{r, outcome model with T-M interaction}
# Outcome model with T-M interaction and covariate adjustment
out.fit.tm <- lm(test.final_text3_sum ~ practice_type_bi * cognitive.effort_diff +
                       interest_text1 + prior.knowledge_text1 + 
                       episodic.memory_acc + sellmo_learninggoals + 
                       male + diverse + age,
                     data = df)
summary(out.fit.tm)
```

Ignoring the treatment-mediator interaction (between practice type and change in cognitive effort) assumes constant relationships between the key variables of a mediation analysis.

```{r, outcome model without T-M interaction}
# cf) Outcome model with only covariates and without T-M interaction
out.fit.cov.only <- lm(test.final_text3_sum ~ practice_type_bi + cognitive.effort_diff +
                       interest_text1 + prior.knowledge_text1 + 
                       episodic.memory_acc + sellmo_learninggoals + 
                       male + diverse + age,
                     data = df)
summary(out.fit.cov.only)
```

## (In)direct effect estimation (Table 3)

(In)direct effects are estimated based on estimates from the mediator and outcome models. Confidence intervals are estimated using the bias corrected and accelerated (BCa) bootstrap with 10,000 bootstrap samples. A seed is specified for replication purposes.

Among the results, we examine

- ACME (control): Standalone indirect effect
- ACME (treated): Complementary indirect effect
- ADE (treated): Complementary direct effect

, supporting FTE-specific research questions. 

```{r, (in)direct effect estimation}
# Estimate mediation effects using mediation::mediate()
# Seed setting is needed because it relies on Monte Carlo draws of potential mediators/outcomes
set.seed(54321)
med.estimation <- mediate(med.fit, out.fit.tm, 
                          treat = "practice_type_bi", 
                          mediator = "cognitive.effort_diff", 
                          boot = TRUE, boot.ci.type = "bca", sims = 10000)
summary(med.estimation)
```

## Sensitivity analysis (Figure 6)

We complement our mediation analysis with a series of sensitivity analyses on the degree of omitted confounding between the mediator and outcome, represented by the sensitivity parameter $\rho$ (Imai, Keele, Tingley, 2010, Psychological Methods).

```{r, sensitivity analysis}
# Sensitivity analysis for M-Y confounders
set.seed(12345)
sens.out <- medsens(med.estimation, rho.by = 0.1, sims = 10000, 
                    effect.type = "both")
summary(sens.out)
```

Based on the sensitivity analysis results, we can draw sensitivity plots for our (in)direct effect estimates. Among these, we examine

- $ACME_0(\rho)$: Standalone indirect effect
- $ACME_1(\rho)$: Complementary indirect effect
- $ADE_1(\rho)$: Complementary direct effect

```{r, sensitivity plots}
# Sensitivity plots
plot(sens.out, sens.par = "rho")
```
